questions.q: A patient typically experiences bloating and gas after consuming milk products. This is likely due to a deficiency in which brush border enzyme?
questions.explain: Lactose intolerance is caused by a deficiency in lactase, the enzyme required to digest lactose (milk sugar). Undigested lactose ferments in the colon, causing gas and bloating.

questions.q: If the sphincter of Oddi is blocked, which phase of digestion is most severely compromised?
options: Digestion of lipids in the small intestine
Absorption of water in the colon
Acidification of the bolus in the stomach
questions.explain: The sphincter of Oddi controls the flow of digestive juices (bile and pancreatic enzymes) into the duodenum. Blockage prevents bile (lipid emulsification) and pancreatic lipase (lipid digestion) from entering, severely compromising fat digestion.

questions.q: After absorption into the enterocyte, monoglycerides and long-chain fatty acids are reassembled into triglycerides. Which structure packages them for transport into the lymph?
questions.explain: Inside the enterocyte, lipids are reassembled into triglycerides and packaged with proteins into chylomicrons, which are too large for capillaries and enter the lacteals (lymph).

questions.q: Which component of pancreatic juice is necessary to neutralize the acidic chyme entering the duodenum from the stomach?
questions.explain: Sodium bicarbonate is secreted by the pancreas to neutralize gastric acid, creating a neutral or slightly alkaline pH required for pancreatic enzymes to function.
